stories.headline: Patriots' 2026 rookies: Who has made an impact through five weeks?
stories.summary: With two rookies assuming starting roles, let's take a look at how this year's draft class has panned out.
stories.body:
FOXBOROUGH, Mass. -- Quick-hit thoughts and notes around the New England Patriots and NFL:

1. Rookie report: The Patriots (355) have had rookies play more snaps on special teams than every team but the Colts (403) entering Week 6 games, according to ESPN Research.

That has been one of the defining characteristics of the team's class of 2026. That also could be changing Sunday when the 3-2 Patriots host the 2-3 New York Jets (1 p.m. ET, CBS), with first-round pick Caleb Lomu possibly set to make his first career NFL start if left tackle Will Campbell's sprained MCL keeps him on the sideline.

Lomu delivered in a pinch when Campbell left last week's 45-17 win over the Raiders early in the second quarter with a sprained right MCL, which provides a timely springboard to highlight the contributions of the Patriots' rookie class so far.

"I feel like he owned that and did a good job of anchoring. He's athletic and he's big," quarterback Drake Maye said of the 6-foot-6, 313-pound Lomu. "You get reminded of guys that played three years and come out of college. I was in the same scenario ... I was really proud of him stepping up."

Up to that point, Lomu's primary role on offense was as a jumbo tight end. His most extended playing time on offense had come in the fourth quarter of a Week 3 blowout loss to the Jaguars, with coach Mike Vrabel saying the idea was to get him experience.

Maye, remembering his own rookie season and trying to fit in with his more experienced teammates, had a message for Lomu.

"I told him after maybe the first or second time we scored with him in there, it's like, 'Hey, we're just playing ball now. Just have some fun'," Maye relayed. "I think that's kind of just a reminder I try to tell the young guys -- once you get in there, you get rolling. After that, you kind of let the nerves settle. It's just playing the same old football."

To his credit, outside linebacker Gabe Jacas, the second-round pick from Illinois, has made the transition look rather seamless after he missed all spring and the initial days of training camp due to a knee procedure and contract stalemate. Jacas has played a rookie-high 60.7% of the defensive snaps, totaling 15 tackles, 1.5 sacks and one interception.

Meanwhile, third-round pick Eli Raridon has played 40% of the offensive snaps and amassed eight receptions for 101 yards and a touchdown. He's the No. 2 tight end behind veteran Hunter Henry, a role he might have had to wait longer to seize if not for a season-ending knee injury sustained by Julian Hill in the spring.

"He's talented," said Vrabel, who previously noted Raridon (6-6, 245) became a better blocker quicker than anticipated. "He's continuing to get more comfortable each and every day, that he sees what this league is about, maybe starts to have more confidence in himself that he can do this at this level and he can do it fairly well."

Vrabel also noted that fifth-round pick Karon Prunty, a cornerback out of Wake Forest, had been gaining confidence as a gunner on special teams before a hamstring injury has sidelined him the last two games.

Furthermore, linebacker Namdi Obiazor (sixth-round pick out of TCU) has played 104 special teams snaps and is tied for the team-lead with fellow rookie Erick Hunter (undrafted) with six tackles.

Other rookie contributors on special teams have included undrafted rookies Channing Canada and Tanner Arkin, while offensive tackle Dametrious Crownover (sixth-round, Texas A&M) and quarterback Behren Morton (seventh-round, Texas Tech) have been developing behind the scenes.

One point Vrabel has made in the past is how significant the leap is from college to the NFL, which he referenced Friday when asked what has stood out to him from the class.

"I think they've improved and played for us in some good spots. They're 21-, 22-year-old kids, so it's good to see them improve, and we have to invest in those guys. We can't lose sight of them [even though] they aren't playing 80% of the snaps," he said.

"We have to continue to do that, and that's exciting. They're very coachable. Much more coachable than some of the veterans, that's why I like coaching them."

2. Maye vs. blitz: When assessing the Jets' defense, offensive coordinator Josh McDaniels said, "They blitz. And blitz. And blitz."

The Jets have sent five or more rushers 41% of the time (No. 3 in the NFL), according to ESPN Research, and Maye has a 63 QBR vs. the blitz, which ranks 15th. It will be a key part of Sunday's matchup.

3. AVT reunion: Left guard Alijah Vera-Tucker said he's approaching the game against the his former team like any other week, although the presence of close friends on the Jets' sideline naturally adds a twist after he spent the first five years of his career there.

Vera-Tucker has played every snap this season and ranks 18th among NFL interior offensive linemen in pass block win rate (92%). Vrabel said one thing that has stood out to him about Vera-Tucker is that "it's really meant a lot to him; I can see that in the way he prepares and responds."

4. Milton sees double: Defensive tackle Milton Williams isn't filling up the stat sheet (11 tackles, no sacks), although that didn't stop ESPN NFL analyst Dan Orlovsky from asking last week if he is the NFL's best at his position. The analysis was timely, as Patriots defensive coordinator Zak Kuhr noted Williams has been seeing more double-teams, and Williams shared he's handling that better mentally than he was earlier in the season.

"I felt like the first couple weeks I was in my own head about it, making excuses, instead of going out and playing," he said.

5. Morton perspective: Rookie quarterback Behren Morton, the Eastland, Texas, native who attended Texas Tech, touched on three topics this week:

Impressions of New England region: "It's beautiful. The spring was awesome, and you actually get a true fall. That's something I never got in Texas, because it usually goes summer straight into winter. Seeing the leaves turn, get the fall feeling, it's football season. The people have been great up here. I've really enjoyed it and my fiancée is up here now, too, and we've really enjoyed the Northeast, for sure."
What stands out football-wise: "It feels like I've been here for 20 years already, the amount of time processing the playbook. It's a lot [different] than a college playbook, especially coming from Texas Tech, the no-huddle situation, always in the gun. Coach McDaniels has brought a different side of football to me. Your football IQ can't help but go through the roof learning from him and getting to watch all the years of Tom [Brady] doing it. It's the same offense, so you can learn so much. There's an endless amount of film."
Scout-team QB role: "Go back to Josh Allen. That week was awesome. I knew that we had to have a get-back-on-track game for us, so always trying to put my best foot forward in game prep -- whatever I could do for the defense with little tricks of the trade that Josh does. Because he does some different stuff. Then getting the win on Sunday, that makes you feel a lot better, too."

6. Vrabel's sarcasm: The Patriots are one of four teams with a turnover in every game this season (11 overall) entering Week 6 games, joining the Broncos, Raiders and Chargers, and Vrabel's sarcasm was evident in an interview on Patriots All-Access. Previewing Sunday's game against the Jets, he cracked, "They've only turned the ball over three times. We can do that in a half."

7. Byard's take: Jets quarterback Geno Smith has yet to throw an interception this season after totaling 17 in 2025, and Patriots safety Kevin Byard made the point he's noticed Smith holding on to the ball longer to avoid those miscues. As a result, Byard noted what could be a key in the game, saying, "It gives some opportunities for our pass rushers for sacks and forced fumbles."

The Patriots enter with 11 sacks (tied for 18th in NFL) and five forced fumbles (tied for 17th).

8. Coach Gonzo: Cornerback Christian Gonzalez returns Sunday after missing the last two games with a shoulder injury, but his presence on the sideline was notable in last Sunday's win over the Raiders. He said it was important to him to be there for his teammates and share tendencies he saw from the offense as he works to "grow vocals and trying to lead." Gonzalez added he was looking forward to facing Jets No. 1 receiver Garrett Wilson on Sunday.

9. Did You Know, Part I: The Patriots have posted 11 wins over the Jets by 30 or more points, the most by any team against a single opponent in the Super Bowl era (since 1966). The next highest is nine -- by the 49ers over the Falcons.

10. Did You Know, Part II: The Patriots have had rookies play a total of 818 snaps entering Week 6 games, which ranks 15th in the NFL. The Dolphins (2,090) easily lead the NFL in snaps played by rookies, followed by the Browns (1,401), Chargers (1,301), Giants (1,246), Ravens (1,101) and Buccaneers (992), according to ESPN Research.

stories.headline: Rays' big three of Caminero, Diaz, Aranda deliver big hits in ALCS Game 4 win
stories.summary: Junior Caminero, Yandy Diaz and Jonathan Aranda combined to go 6-for-14 with five RBIs as the Rays tied the ALCS at 2-2 with Saturday's 7-3 win over Cleveland.
stories.body:
CLEVELAND -- The Tampa Bay Rays' big three, the trio of hitters the franchise needs to fuel its first championship run, heard the ribbing from manager Kevin Cash before their 7-3 win over the Cleveland Guardians in Game 4 of the American League Championship Series.

They heard it in the cage Friday while they waited out a rain delay that became a rainout and again Saturday as they prepared to play on a frigid night at Progressive Field.

Third baseman Junior Caminero, designated hitter Yandy Diaz and first baseman Jonathan Aranda carried the offense to 98 wins and an AL East title and through a sweep of the New York Yankees in the AL Division Series. But the few times they've collectively struggled this season, such as over the first three games of this ALCS, Cash busted out a different nickname to loosen them up.

The big three? More like Los Tres Pequeno's -- the three little ones.

"It's kind of a dig at them and protecting the rest of the lineup," Cash said. "So when they don't hit on a given night, I'm like, 'Yeah, I got my three Pequeno's hitting.' Yandy, Cammy and Aranda, they've all heard it."

Los Pequeno's came up huge Saturday as the Rays evened the series at two games apiece and ensured it will return home to Florida for Game 6 on Monday, combining to go 6-for-14 with five RBIs.

"Los Tres Pequeno's right there," Caminero said. "Pretty good job today for the boys."

The barrel-chested Diaz, who was the most productive of the three stars with three hits in the first three games, went 2-for-5 with a two-run home run that carried just over the wall in right field in the ninth inning to put the finishing touches on the victory.

Aranda, who entered Saturday 0-for-10 in the series, finished 3-for-4, including a single in the seventh inning that scored two runs thanks to Guardians right fielder Chase DeLauter allowing the ball to roll under his glove. Aranda wound up at third base on the error and scored moments later on Chandler Simpson's sacrifice fly.

Then there's Caminero, the franchise's 23-year-old cornerstone and AL MVP candidate who went 0-for-4 with four strikeouts in Game 3 as the Rays, the team with the lowest strikeout rate in the majors this season, fanned 13 times in a 3-2 loss. It was just Caminero's second career four-strikeout performance. The struggle was jarring to outsiders. He remained confident.

"Everybody knows me," Caminero said. "Everybody was confused about the four strikeouts and I said, 'No, no. I know who I am.' Everybody knows who I am. Everybody here gave me the support."

He responded Saturday by launching a pair of blistering line drives.

The first was a 110.7 mph flyball to center field with a 29-degree launch angle that went 410 feet and was somehow caught by Petey Halpin at the wall in the third inning. The ball had a 1.000 expected batting average and would've been a home run in 17 of 30 ballparks. It was the 204th ball in the Statcast Era (since 2015) that was hit at least 110 mph with that launch angle, and the first not to be hit for a home run, according to ESPN Research.

Caminero said he "100%" thought it was a home run, which would've given the Rays a 2-1 lead. Instead, he gave it to them in the sixth inning when he cracked a 110.2 mph line drive into the left-field corner for an RBI double. When he reached second base, after pounding his chest and releasing a scream, he put his index finger on his lips as if to shush the noise.

"Junior is great, and now it's his turn to be great in the postseason," Cash said. "Today was a big step in the right direction for him. I wouldn't be surprised now if he catches fire and does a lot for us."

On the mound, Nick Martinez continued his success on the road in 2026 -- he posted a 2.38 ERA in 16 starts away from Tropicana Field during the regular season -- by holding the Guardians to one run on two hits over 5⅓ innings. Freddy Peralta, the Rays' Game 2 starter and presumptive Game 6 starter, replaced him in the sixth inning for his first relief appearance since 2024. Peralta entered with one out and a runner at first base and worked around a walk to escape the jam on nine pitches.

"He was all eager to come in and do it," Cash said. "Then showed why. I mean, a lot of power. Got huge outs for us."

Ian Seymour stumbled in the seventh inning, surrendering two runs on four hits, before Kevin Kelly, Cam Booser and Bryan Baker combined for two scoreless innings. Díaz supplied the final cushion with his first home run of the postseason in the final frame.

Drew Rasmussen, Tampa Bay's ace, will take the mound Sunday afternoon opposite All-Star rookie left-hander Parker Messick. Teams that have won Game 5 in a series tied at two games apiece are 46-23, a 67% clip. The Rays' chances will only grow if their Pequeno's continue producing.

"At some point you think they're going to deliver, and they do," Booser said. "So it's good to see them get back on track and good to see us get back playing our ball."

stories.headline: Jasmine Jasudavicius outpoints Erin Blanchfield at UFC Fight Night
stories.summary: Jasmine Jasudavicius stated her case as a contender in the UFC women's featherweight division, dominating Erin Blanchfield on the canvas to win by unanimous decision Saturday.
stories.body:
Instability and opportunity permeate the UFC women's flyweight division, which crowned a new champion two weeks ago and has a former two-time champ lurking in the wings while healing from injury. Several other title hopefuls have been jostling to position themselves to go for the gold.

Jasmine Jasudavicius seized the opportunity to make her presence felt among the leading contenders Saturday, dominating Erin Blanchfield on the canvas in a clash of top-10 125-pounders to win by unanimous decision at UFC Fight Night in Edmonton, Alberta.

The fight was the co-main event of a card headlined by Mike Malott's explosive knockout win over Joaquin Buckley. Malott, who like Jasudavicius is from Ontario and had the crowd firmly behind him, landed a knee to the chin that crumbled Buckley, who is No. 8 in the ESPN welterweight rankings and lost his third in a row.

"Hey, guys, I might be soft-spoken," Malott said afterward, "but I'm f---ing hard-hitting."

Malott's knockout came at 2 minutes, 32 seconds of the second round and put a ferocious cap on an event that tied a UFC record with 12 finishes (seven knockouts, five submissions). The other modern-era fight card with a dozen finishes was UFC Fight Night in Belgrade, Serbia, on Aug. 1.

Nevertheless, it was the night's lone bout to go the distance that had the highest stakes. Jasudavicius, No. 8 in the ESPN women's flyweight rankings, pulled off the upset against third-ranked Blanchfield, who came in situated behind only injured former champion Valentina Shevchenko and new titlist Natalia Silva. Blanchfield is also No. 9 in the ESPN women's pound-for-pound top 10.

Jasudavicius (16-4) surely elevated her standing in the 125-pound hierarchy with a robust performance that produced her second straight victory. Both women came in touted as elite grapplers, and Jasudavicius proved to be a step ahead by repeatedly taking the fight to the ground (five takedowns) and threatening submissions from dominant positions for long stretches of the first two rounds.

"I love grappling," she said. "I understand it. I'm pretty good at it. And I like to show what I've got."

Jasudavicius showed enough to impress the judges, getting the nod on all three scorecards (29-28, 29-28, 29-28). The announcement of the verdict drew a roar from the crowd, which was enthusiastically behind the 37-year-old competing in her home country.

"To be able to fight in Canada, you hear the crowd, man. We're about it," Jasudavicius said.

Jasudavicius and Malott were among a dozen Canadian fighters on the card, who went a combined 5-7.

Jasudavicius' victory might not put her in position for an immediate title shot, but she has her sights on a future meeting with the new champ, who defeated her by decision in 2022 in her second UFC fight.

"I want to cross paths with Natalia Silva again," Jasudavicius said. "We had a little bit of history before, so it would be an epic story."

For Blanchfield (14-3), the defeat halted a two-fight winning streak. She outlanded Jasudavicius 62-43 in significant strikes, but the author of five UFC submissions never could get her ground game going. Jasudavicius put Blanchfield on the defensive the whole fight with nearly eight minutes of control time.

stories.headline: Lionel Messi scores twice, takes season tally to 25 in Miami win at Atlanta
stories.summary: Lionel Messi scored two scintillating second-half solo goals to take his MLS-leading tally to 25 as Inter Miami brushed aside hosts Atlanta United 3-1 on Saturday.
stories.body:
Lionel Messi scored two trademark second-half solo goals to take his MLS-leading tally to 25 as Inter Miami brushed aside hosts Atlanta United 3-1 on Saturday.

After Mexico striker Germán Berterame put Miami ahead in the 45th minute, Messi took center stage after the restart with two goals in four minutes.

The first, in the 56th minute, came after Messi drove infield from the right wing and exchanged passes with Berterame on the edge off the penalty area before dancing past a desperate Atlanta defender and firing low into the net.

His second was more of the same. This time, Luis Suárez sent him free on a breakaway and the Argentine forward again bewitched a hapless defender before once more beating Atlanta goalkeeper Lucas Hoyos with his left foot.

Atlanta got a late consolation goal through a penalty from former Miami forward Fafà Picault.

"He never ceases to amaze the world," Miami coach Cristian "Kily" González said of Messi afterward. "I mean, I honestly can't believe that a guy like him, at 39 years old, is doing what he's doing. And what makes me happiest is seeing that he's truly happy. Because he's happy, he gives everything he has. He enjoys himself and feels right at home.

"As I always say, he pushes us to be better every single day. It's an immense joy to have him here. Everyone knows how special our relationship is. Every time I see him, he brings a smile to my face. I'm still constantly amazed by him."

At full time of Saturday's game, Messi had a six-goal lead in the race for MLS' Golden Boot and also had the joint-most assists (15), along with LAFC's Son Heung-Min, having been credited with a secondary assist on Berterame's opener.

Messi is the first player in MLS history to register 15 assists in three consecutive seasons. He now has a goal contribution in 13 straight matches, tying his second-longest streak with club and country in his career.

Saturday's brace also took Messi to 936 career goals, and his coach has no doubts that he can reach the 1,000 milestone.

"Yes, I believe he'll reach 1,000 goals," González said. "I have faith in that. I know he will, because he loves a challenge, he sets challenges for himself and since he's already achieved everything else, this will be no exception."

He added: "He dazzles me with every single action, every time I see him in training. I truly hope he continues to amaze us right up until the day he decides to retire, which, hopefully, won't be for a long time yet."

Messi's performance Saturday gave the eight-time Ballon d'Or winner another fond memory at Atlanta's Mercedes-Benz Stadium. The game marked Messi's first visit there since the 2026 World Cup semifinal in July, when he provided two late assists to propel Argentina to a dramatic win over England.

Messi has four goals in three games since he bid farewell to the Argentina national team in a friendly against Benin earlier this month.

Miami, which clinched a spot in the playoffs Wednesday, has won three straight games and is second in the Eastern Conference behind runaway leader Nashville.

Atlanta, under Gerardo "Tata" Martino, Messi's former coach with Miami and Argentina, is languishing in the 14th spot in the Eastern Conference and facing an uphill battle to make the postseason.

Miami will return to action with a visit to the New York Red Bulls next Saturday.

ESPN's Lizzy Becherano contributed to this report.

stories.headline: Chelsea's Emi Martínez has surgery, will be 'back in a few weeks'
stories.summary: Emi Martínez said he would be "back in a few weeks" after undergoing surgery following a head injury suffered during Chelsea's Premier League win over Everton on Saturday.
stories.body:
Emi Martínez said he would be "back in a few weeks" after undergoing surgery following a head injury suffered during Chelsea's Premier League win over Everton on Saturday.

Martínez, 34, collided with Everton's Jarrad Branthwaite when rushing from his goal to attempt to punch an Everton free kick out of his penalty area in the 67th minute of Chelsea's 2-0 win at the Hill Dickinson Stadium.

Both players received treatment on the pitch, with the Everton defender recovering quickly. Martínez, however, received extended treatment from the Chelsea physios and paramedics before being stretchered from the field while receiving oxygen.

He was replaced by 21-year-old substitute goalkeeper Mike Penders in the 75th minute. Eleven minutes of injury time were added on by the officials at the end of the match following the lengthy stoppage in play.

The Argentina goalkeeper posted a photo of himself in a hospital bed late Saturday night, with the caption: "Thank you all for the messages, the operation went well. The most important thing is that we won and with a bow at 0. We'll be back in a few weeks."

Chelsea coach Xabi Alonso earlier told reporters that Martínez was conscious when leaving the stadium and was taken to hospital for "precautionary tests," adding: "For now, we need to wait."

He added: "It was a concussion, but more than that. I saw just one clip, but we'll have to wait."

Two goals from Pedro Neto ensured Chelsea took all three points from their trip to Merseyside.

"We are really pleased. Shame for Emi, but we wish you all the best. This win is for him," Neto told TNT Sports.

Everton manager David Moyes said: "I just said to TV, I've not seen the Martínez injury yet, so I hope he's fine. I really do. I couldn't even see from the dugout. It just looked as if it was a sharing ball in between a couple of people. I don't know what else happened."

Chelsea's victory put an end to Everton's unbeaten start to the campaign and saw their defense hold firm for the first time this season.

"I'm really pleased with the performance, with the win, with the clean sheet," Alonso said. "There are many positives to build on from today. We knew it was going to be a hard challenge to win in this stadium, but we did many things to deserve the win. I think we got many things right. We were very professional, very solid, and it's good to have this feeling to win this way.

"We needed to feel like we could win in this way -- being solid, being strong, looking in control and going through difficult moments.

"In the first half, there were moments where there were corners and throw-ins and you need to overcome these moments. It's very hard in the Premier League to have full control of the game but you need to make sure you don't lose your shape or your condition, and today we did that really well."

Information from ESPN's Beth Lindop contributed to this story.

stories.headline: Knicks waive Bruce Brown, keep James Wiseman ahead of opener
stories.summary: The Knicks are waiving Bruce Brown and keeping James Wiseman on the roster as the team heads into its regular-season opener, sources told ESPN.
stories.body:
The New York Knicks waived Bruce Brown and will keep James Wiseman on the roster as the team heads into its regular-season opener.

Brown was one of several players on non-guaranteed deals vying for one of New York's final two available roster spots. Tony Bradley, Ochai Agbaji and Drew Eubanks also were waived in recent days.

Wiseman appeared in all four of the Knicks' preseason games and impressed in 24 minutes versus the Toronto Raptors on Tuesday, when he scored 18 points and grabbed 10 rebounds.

According to ESPN's Bobby Marks, the Knicks could have kept Brown and Wiseman, but because they are only $3.2 million below their self-imposed hard cap at the second apron, retaining both players would've been difficult.

Wiseman, 25, will join Karl-Anthony Towns and Andre Drummond in New York's center rotation. The reigning NBA champions lost key reserve big man Mitchell Robinson to the Boston Celtics this past summer via free agency.

The Knicks will begin the NBA's regular season Tuesday when they host the new-look Philadelphia 76ers.

stories.headline: Christian Horner plays down Ferrari links, 'no idea' on Formula 1 return
stories.summary: Christian Horner again played down links to Ferrari as the former Red Bull boss claimed he would be "at peace" if a return to Formula One never happens.
stories.body:
Christian Horner again played down links to Ferrari as the former Red Bull boss claimed he would be "at peace" if a return to Formula One never happens.

Horner, 52, started his speaking tour to help launch his new book, entitled "Drive," at the Barbican in York on Saturday.

He ran through his entire Formula One career, from Red Bull's introduction into the sport through to his controversial exit after the British Grand Prix in 2025.

- Horner: Mercedes' Wolff has it 'easy' at the moment

- Rafael Câmara to Haas: How F1's next rookie could shake up Ferrari's future

- Verstappen finishes 9th in GT World Challenge

But the two-hour show passed without a single mention of the allegations Horner faced during his latter days with the team. The billed Q&A from the audience was delivered in the form of QR-code submitted questions put to Horner by the host.

Red Bull's decision to sack him came a year and a half after he was accused of "inappropriate behaviour" by a female colleague. Horner always denied the accusations and was exonerated for a second time of controlling behaviour by an independent KC. It is a subject covered in the book in a chapter titled "Out come the wolves."

Horner's Red Bull exit ended a 20-year career with the team, where he won eight drivers' and six constructors' titles, and he continues to be linked with a return to the sport.

A recent interview, in which Horner described Ferrari as the biggest brand in F1, reignited links to the Italian giants, but he again moved to talk that down.

"I said 'there's an aura around Ferrari, it's a privilege as a driver, an engineer etc. It is the dream of so many drivers.' I never said it was my bloody dream!" Horner said.

"But the story came out that Ferrari was my dream job. I felt sorry for Fred [Vasseur, Ferrari team principal] because suddenly he was under a lot of pressure."

Horner touched on how he lured design guru Adrian Newey to the team, his relationship with world champion drivers Sebastian Vettel and Max Verstappen and how the organisation of the team changed following the death of Red Bull co-founder Dietrich Mateschitz in 2022.

He described his sacking from Red Bull, days after the Silverstone race, as "brutal."

When the subject of his future came up again, Horner suggested that a return to F1 is not a certainty.

"What excites me most is what is the next chapter going to be and, honestly, I have no idea," Horner added.

"If my time is done in Formula One, I've had a hell of a ride and I did OK. If the right thing comes up to go back, I go back. But I am at peace in myself that if it doesn't I don't have to."

Red Bull are using their own power trains for the first time this season, the culmination of a five-year project launched in 2021 and overseen by Horner until his departure.

Verstappen has won the last two races -- in Malaysia and Singapore -- to deliver the first successes of that project on track and Horner spoke of his pride in seeing the engine come to fruition.

"Seeing that engine come to life and deliver and be reliable ... people thought it would be a joke," he said.

"To see podiums and then the victories in the last two weeks, in its 16th race to win a Grand Prix, I took huge pride in that. Both shareholders contacted me and thanked me."

stories.headline: Lisandro Martínez's Man United comments 'not that far off' but should not have been made - Peter Schmeichel
stories.summary: Former Manchester United goalkeeper Peter Schmeichel has said he believes Lisandro Martínez's criticism of the club's hierarchy is "not that far off."
stories.body:
Former Manchester United goalkeeper Peter Schmeichel has said he believes Lisandro Martínez's criticism of the club's hierarchy is "not that far off" but added he would not have liked hearing a teammate sound off in public.

Schmeichel was criticised for his handling of a post-match interview with Martínez in the aftermath of Tuesday night's 2-0 Champions League loss to Atlético Madrid, when the Argentina defender turned his fire on the club's hierarchy and named director of football Jason Wilcox as one of those from whom he "expects more."

Martínez spoke first to Amazon Prime's Gabriel Clarke before Schmeichel interviewed him for U.S. broadcaster CBS, with the defender repeating many of his criticisms while Schmeichel appeared to be trying to move Martínez on from the topic.

On Thursday Martínez issued a public apology for his comments and United said the matter was considered closed after the 28-year-old met with manager Michael Carrick, Wilcox and the club's hierarchy.

But inevitably the issue dominated Carrick's news conference on Friday with the substance of Martínez's comments still being debated.

Speaking on The Overlap Daily, Schmeichel said: "I would not like any teammate ever to go out and talk like that. Unless it was Bryan Robson... No, I wouldn't. I absolutely wouldn't like that.

"In the dressing rooms I was in, you were accountable. It just didn't happen very often that somebody stepped out of line, and of course we had a manager [Sir Alex Ferguson] who would not allow you to step out of line. He would react to that straight away...

"It's not that I completely disagree with what [Martínez] says. That's the other thing."

- Man United 'a circus' amid Lisandro Martínez rant - Roy Keane

Schmeichel then added: "Without going into too much detail about what Martínez said, some of the things he said are not far off.

"Look at the promising teams: Manchester City a long time ago, Arsenal for the past six years, Liverpool under Jürgen Klopp -- what did they do that suddenly changed the dynamics and changed their fortunes? They started at the back.

"They got in a goalkeeper, back four, a centre midfield player. They built that foundation, made it solid, and then they started to bring the creative players in. They've all done it... Built from the back. We've done the opposite, built from the front."

stories.headline: NRL transfer whispers: Rivals keeping tabs on Dragons' Tu
stories.summary: The NRL season may be over, but the player market is already heating up ahead of November 1. Isaac Issa has news from the Dragons on some key outside backs
stories.body:
The NRL season may be over, but the player market is already heating up ahead of November 1, with clubs beginning to shape their rosters for 2027 and beyond.

From player movement to changes behind the scenes, ESPN NRL Insider Isaac Issa has the latest whispers from around the competition.

Rivals keeping tabs on Dragons' Tu

Multiple clubs are monitoring St George Illawarra outside back Setu Tu, with the Dragons yet to begin talks over a contract extension.

Tu is contracted until the end of 2027 and is expected to test the open market from November 1, when rival clubs can negotiate a deal for 2028 and beyond.

The former Warriors outside back joined the Dragons on a development contract this season and is set to move into the club's top 30 squad in 2027.

His ability to cover multiple positions across the backline adds to his appeal as clubs assess their recruitment options.

Rivals monitor Patea as open market looms
Penrith young gun Luron Patea is expected to test the open market from November 1, with multiple clubs keeping tabs on the promising prop.

Patea is contracted until the end of 2027, but the Panthers are yet to begin talks over an extension, leaving rival clubs poised to explore a deal for 2028 and beyond.

Penrith have not granted Patea permission to negotiate with other clubs before November 1.

The Panthers junior made his NRL debut in 2024 and has shown promise during his first-grade opportunities, providing another emerging option in Penrith's forward pack.

He is among several Panthers players approaching the final year of their contracts, with veteran prop Moses Leota also unsigned beyond 2027.

Roosters eye Dockar-Clay reunion
The Roosters have shown interest in a potential return for Zach Dockar-Clay as they explore options to bolster their hooking and utility depth.

ESPN understands the 31-year-old has emerged as an option following his departure from Manly, with discussions remaining at an early stage.

Dockar-Clay spent the 2024 and 2025 seasons with the Roosters before joining the Sea Eagles on a one-year deal for 2026.

Manly confirmed his departure last month after a season in which he claimed the club's NSW Cup best-and-fairest award.

Bostock brushes Dragons links

Dolphins star Jack Bostock has dismissed recent links between himself and the Dragons, admitting this isn't the first time he'd been floated for a club switch.

"I've been linked to a few a clubs," Bostock admitted.

"I don't know about [the Dragons links]."

He said that while he "obviously sees it in the media," his sole focus is the Kangaroos.

Sloan's Dragons stay still a possibility

Tyrell Sloan could yet remain at St George Illawarra next season, with discussions ongoing over a potential stay despite his planned move to Castleford.

There is interest in keeping Sloan at the Dragons, but several hurdles remain before that can become a reality.

Roster space and salary cap room would need to be worked through, while any arrangement would also require Castleford to agree to release him.

Sloan previously admitted he would "love to" remain in the NRL when speaking to Channel Nine in August, after his Castleford deal had been announced.

No agreement has been reached and a stay is far from guaranteed.

stories.headline: Jets great Mark Gastineau wants rookie David Bailey to celebrate after sacks
stories.summary: Gastineau's sack dances led to the NFL penalizing excessive celebrations for over 30 years.
stories.body:
FOXBOROUGH, Mass. -- A look at what's happening around the New York Jets:

1. Observations from the sack king: When Mark Gastineau sacked a quarterback, he danced. He danced so much and so flamboyantly that it enraged opponents and annoyed some teammates. How did he react?

More sacks and more dancing ... until the NFL banned excessive individual celebrations in 1984 -- aka the Mark Gastineau Rule, which was officially relaxed in 2017.

Gastineau, 69, believes his famous sack dance was a celebration of joy, hard work paying off, which is why he was surprised to see Jets rookie pass rusher David Bailey react so nonchalantly last Sunday after each of his three sacks against the Cleveland Browns.

"He might be a humble guy," Gastineau told ESPN. "I was humble. Actually, I wasn't [he laughed], but I worked my ass off. My payoff was the celebration. I just got excited, loving every minute of it. I couldn't help but dance.

"I'm sure [Bailey] gets excited. If he doesn't get excited after a sack, that would amaze me. I would find that hard to believe because he knows how hard it is to get back there. He just does his own thing, I guess. That's why there are different people in this world."

Gastineau recorded 107.5 sacks in his career, including 22 in 1984 -- the league's single-season record that stood for 17 years. Watching Bailey, he sees a young player with "a very bright future."

"He played his butt off [last week]," Gastineau said. "I love the way he played."

If Gastineau had the chance, he'd like to ask Bailey this question: Do you get excited about a sack? Bailey might have provided the answer in training camp, when he said a sack is "literally probably the best feeling in the world. It's like nothing else."

He simply chooses to skip the celly, as the kids like to say.

A silver lining, according to Gastineau: "The offensive linemen won't be as apt to get mad, with him not dancing."

2. Big man, fast feet: A 242-pound running back is supposed to be a battering ram, a between-the-tackles menace, but Braelon Allen is shattering that stereotype.

He's deceptively fast, allowing him to gain 4.2 yards per carry and two touchdowns on outside rushes, per Next Gen Stats -- slightly better than starter Breece Hall (3.8 and one TD). Offensive coordinator Frank Reich described Allen as a big man "with little man's feet."

With Hall (quadriceps) sidelined for the third straight game, Allen will be the starting running back again Sunday against the New England Patriots. There's a good chance Hall returns next week, setting up an interesting situation.

"We've said it from the start: We think we have the best one-two combination in the NFL," Reich said.

3. He said what? Wide receiver Tim Patrick raised eyebrows this week when he said the Jets "could be the best" offense in the league.

"We have so much talent, it's insane," he said.

Mind you, Patrick played for the 2024 Detroit Lions, who scored a league-high 564 points. When the quote was relayed to Garrett Wilson, the Jets' top receiver didn't flinch.

"He's been on high-powered offenses ... so he's got a great grasp of what it looks like," Wilson said. "So it's definitely high praise coming from him. When I hear that, it's like, 'All right, now we have to back that up.'"

4. Did you know? Since the merger in 1970, only three Jets quarterbacks have recorded at least two regular-season wins against the Patriots -- Vinny Testaverde (three), Chad Pennington (two) and Mark Sanchez (two). Geno Smith can join the group. He was on the winning side as a rookie in 2013.

5. The more you can do ... Will McDonald IV is a former first-round pick who has gone from every-down player to situational pass rusher. It has resulted in a fairly significant drop in playing time, but he's picking up snaps on special teams. In fact, he's on the kickoff coverage unit for the first time since his rookie year in 2023.

It started two weeks ago, and he responded nicely last week, with two tackles against the Browns. McDonald received praise from Glenn, who noted that McDonald wanted to be part of special teams. They also had an opening when edge defender Braiden McGregor went down because of a season-ending pectoral injury.

McDonald was also deployed last week as a spy on Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson. It wouldn't be a surprise if the Jets use him the same way against the Patriots' Drake Maye. McDonald has a unique skill set, and the Jets are finding ways to utilize it.

6. A player to watch: Rookie defensive tackle Darrell Jackson Jr. has received a gradual increase in his playing time, and that figures to continue after a four-tackle, one-sack performance last week -- easily his best game. He's part of a four-man interior rotation, along with T'Vondre Sweat, Harrison Phillips and Jowon Briggs.

7. Talkin' about practice: For the second week in a row, Glenn held a walk-through practice Wednesday, not a full practice. It was understandable last week, coming off an 89-play outing by the defense. But why again?

Glenn didn't elaborate, saying only that it was best for the team. The players appreciate the walk-throughs because they reduce the wear and tear on their bodies while allowing them to focus on mental preparation. One player estimated that they run twice as many plays in a walk-through as regular practice, just without pads.

Old-school coaches like to practice in pads because they believe it sharpens fundamentals, especially for linemen, while maintaining a physical mindset. Glenn has embraced new-school approaches, incorporating player feedback into his decisions. The players say it builds trust.

It works nicely ... as long as they perform on Sundays.

8. The Brownlee blitz: Nickel back Jarvis Brownlee Jr. probably won't challenge Bailey for the team sack lead, but he's making some noise as a blitzer. He has already rushed 21 times, double his total from his first two seasons (including 19 games with the Tennessee Titans).

"I actually enjoy it, I really enjoy it," Brownless said. "It just gives me confidence and shows that A.G. and the guys upstairs believe in my abilities and what I can do."

Brownlee's slot blitz backfired in Week 3, as the Lions' Jahmyr Gibbs slipped out of the backfield for a game-winning touchdown reception. Overall, Brownlee has two quarterback hits, including one sack.

9. Hello, friend: Another week, another popular former Jet on the schedule.

Last week, it was Browns linebacker Quincy Williams, who wreaked havoc with three forced fumbles. This time, it's guard Alijah Vera-Tucker, who, like Williams, left via free agency last offseason.

The Jets, concerned about Vera-Tucker's extensive injury history, didn't make a strong bid to retain him. The feeling apparently was mutual, as he noted a desire to get a fresh start. He wound up signing a three-year, $42 million contract in New England, where he hasn't missed a snap in five games -- the only Patriots offensive player to do so.

10. The last word: Thursday marked the 10th anniversary of Dennis Byrd's tragic death. The former Jets defensive lineman, whose career was cut short when he suffered a broken neck on the field in 1992, causing temporary paralysis and a lifetime of impaired walking. He died Oct. 15, 2016, in a two-car accident in Oklahoma at the age of 50.

One of Byrd's last public appearances was at Gillette Stadium for the 2010 AFC divisional playoff game. The night before, he gave a motivational speech to the Jets, who lauded his inspirational message. After upsetting the Patriots, linebacker Bart Scott said, "For him to be walking today is a miracle. How can you not listen to a miracle?"

stories.headline: DeLauter's costly error deflates Guardians' hopes as Rays even ALCS in Game 4
stories.summary: Chase DeLauter's error in right field opened the door for the Rays in the pivotal seventh inning, and Tampa Bay went on to win 7-3 to even the ALCS at 2-2.
stories.body:
CLEVELAND -- The Guardians were hoping to stay within striking distance as the Tampa Bay Rays mounted a seventh-inning rally in Game 4 of the American League Championship Series on Saturday, but right fielder Chase DeLauter's error opened the door for a bigger inning.

Already trailing 2-1 with runners on second and third and one out, DeLauter misplayed a Jonathan Aranda single in right field, allowing the ball to get under his glove. Two runs scored on the play while Aranda ended up on third base. Moments later, Aranda scored, too, on Chandler Simpson's sacrifice fly to give Tampa Bay a four-run lead.

"Put that one on me," DeLauter told ESPN after the 7-3 loss. "You miss a ground ball and give up two runs -- essentially give up three. It's my fault he's on third base. It sucks."

It's likely the two runners on base were going to score on the single anyway, but Aranda's unearned run allowed for some cushion as the Guardians got two runs back in the bottom of the inning.

"It looked like it may have snaked on him or just skipped by him, took his eye off of it," manager Stephen Vogt said.

Second baseman Travis Bazzana added: "He's been unreal out there, all year. The numbers would say so, and my eyes would tell us that he's been really solid out there for us."

DeLauter's error probably wasn't a game changer, considering the Rays extended their lead in the ninth, scoring two more times. But that didn't stop DeLauter from wearing it afterward, saying it's something that "can't happen."

"Just missed it," he said. "Ground ball under my glove -- that simple. Tied series. Another home game. Move on and come back and be better tomorrow."

stories.headline: How Golden State held court to take 1-0 lead over Atlanta in WNBA Finals
stories.summary: Golden State held court 68-64 to take a 1-0 lead over the Atlanta Dream in Game 1 of the WNBA Finals.
stories.body:
SAN FRANCISCO -- Game 1 goes to the Golden State Valkyries.

The No. 2 seed held court 68-64 in Game 1 of the WNBA Finals to take the early lead over the No. 4 seed Atlanta Dream in the best-of-seven series.

Gabby Williams led Golden State with 26 points, including four free throws in the final 1:18 to seal the victory. The back-and-forth game featured seven lead changes.

Allisha Gray paced the Dream with 19 points but didn't score in the fourth quarter when the Dream shot 2-for-20 in the period. Angel Reese had 14 points and 12 rebounds.

The Valkyries, who have won all five playoff games at home this postseason and had the best record at home in the regular season, snapped the Dream's 10-game winning streak, which dated to the regular season.

Both teams seek their first WNBA championship. Game 2 is Monday night back at Chase Center. As the better seed, the Valkyries will host Games 2 and, if necessary, 5 and 7 in a 2-2-1-1-1 format.

ESPN was courtside Saturday with live analysis throughout the game.

Jump to:

Postgame analysis | Relive the action

More:

Finals preview | Top 15 players | Schedule | Offseason guide

(2) Golden State Valkyries 68,

(4) Atlanta Dream 64

How Golden State won the game: Both teams made big runs in this game, which set up a fourth quarter that was all about grit and determination. And also timing. After being outscored 17-9 in the third quarter, the Valkyries outscored the Dream 17-8 in the fourth quarter.

The Dream went just 4-of-25 from 3-point range, with Allisha Gray going 1-of-8. They were 18-of-21 from the foul line, but that was an area where the Valkyries were able to make up ground in the fourth quarter, finishing 11-of-16 from the stripe.

Getting into crunch time, Atlanta seemed to get a little too sped up offensively and took shots too early when it would have helped the Dream to work their offense more. Of course, that's easier said than done against the best defense in the WNBA.

Rebounding ended up being a key factor, as the Valkyries won the board battle 41-35. And Golden State's depth -- much talked about before the series began -- came through. Particularly with Kaila Charles, who played 30 minutes, compiling seven points and 10 rebounds.

Gabby Williams led the way with 26 points, the only Valkyries player in double figures. -- Michael Voepel

What the win means for the Valkyries: They won their first Finals game in their first WNBA Finals appearance. Even when the Dream went on runs, the Valkyries never deviated from their game plan -- and it never felt like they fully lost momentum. Maybe that's also a credit to the noise in Ballhalla.

This game showed an elite level of composure from the Valkyries, and that is a great sign for Golden State. Gabby Williams said that even though the Valkyries trailed with a few minutes left in the game, they had the Dream "right where we wanted them." She said it's because they knew the game would come down to stops.

"That's our bread and butter," Williams added.

If the Valkyries can withstand the Dream's offensive runs and then lock them up on defense, they have a good chance to head to Atlanta with a 2-0 lead. -- Kendra Andrews

What changes do you expect in Game 2? The Dream must win a game on the road if they want to win the title, so winning Game 1 would have given them more of a cushion moving forward. Now, Game 2 feels like a must-win at Chase Center before the series shifts to Atlanta for Games 3 and 4.

Dream coach Karl Smesko sounded confident in his team's ability to turn things around in Game 2. He said Saturday's game didn't come down to what Golden State did, but rather the Dream's loss was the result of one bad defensive stretch and a cold offensive quarter in the fourth.

Still, when the Dream punched first in the opening quarter, they led by only eight points at the end of the period. For Atlanta to even the series Monday, the Dream have to make sure they are executing. They also need more from Angel Reese, who dominated early but was held scoreless in the second half, and Rhyne Howard, who finished with 12 points but shot 3-for-14 from the field and 2-for-9 from 3-point range. -- Andrews

stories.summary: Antoine Griezmann had two goals and an assist, Martín Ojeda added a goal and an assist, and Orlando City beat D.C. United 3-1 on Saturday night.
stories.body:
ORLANDO, Fla. -- - Antoine Griezmann had two goals and an assist, Martín Ojeda added a goal and an assist, and Orlando City beat D.C. United 3-1 on Saturday night.

Griezmann has 12 goals and seven assists in 14 MLS appearances and is the first player in league history with a goal contribution in 12 of his first 14 career games.

Marco Pasalić scored a stoppage-time goal for Orlando (12-13-5). Maxime Crépeau had three saves.

Tai Baribo converted from the penalty spot in first-half stoppage time for D.C. (7-10-12).

Ojeda, just inside the top of the 18-yard box, chipped a first-touch pass over four defenders to a charging Griezmann on the give-and-go for a first-touch finish from 7 yards out to make it 1-0 in the 15th minute.

Ojeda flicked a back-heel volley, off a feed from Griezmann, past goalkeeper Sean Johnson and inside the left post to give Orlando a two-goal lead in the 22nd.

Griezmann intercepted a misplayed pass by Kye Rowles in D.C.'s defensive third, took two dribbles and rolled a shot into the net to make it 3-1 in the 50th minute.

Johnson finished with three saves.

stories.headline: Mikel Arteta: 'Big believer' Arsenal's Kai Havertz can score 30 goals a season
stories.summary: Mikel Arteta has said he is a "big believer" that Kai Havertz can be Arsenal's 30-goal-a-season man.
stories.body:
Mikel Arteta has said he is a "big believer" that Kai Havertz can be Arsenal's 30-goal-a-season man.

Havertz is set to lead the line for Arsenal in their clash at Nottingham Forest on Sunday as he continues to be preferred to the out-of-favour Viktor Gyökeres.

The German joined Arsenal from Chelsea in 2023, scoring 14 goals in his first season at the Emirates Stadium before netting 15 in the following campaign.

A hamstring injury saw him miss the concluding four months of that season before both hamstring and knee problems restricted him to just 24 appearances across all competitions last term, with a return of seven goals.

The 27-year-old has started all of Arsenal's league games so far, scoring twice in the Premier League champions' opening three games, but has not found the back of the net since -- a barren streak of five matches.

However, speaking ahead of Sunday's contest at the City Ground, Arteta insisted Havertz can hit as many as 30 goals a season.

"He has that ability," Arteta said. "That is why he is playing there as well, and that is why we signed him.

"He needs that volume of games and actions, and if you give him that, I am a big believer that yes, he can do it.

"His football IQ is something else. He understands everything at such speed, and he can break down information better probably than anyone else on the team.

- Mikel Arteta defends Viktor Gyökeres after goalless start to season

- Mikel Merino: I am 'fortunate to be alive' after Dortmund bus attack

- Eberechi Eze to perform Cristiano Ronaldo-inspired celebration after loss to IShowSpeed

"That's something that's not easy to say especially when we talk about a striker. He was out for a long period of time last season and to get back at the highest level is not easy and it can take time.

"But Kai has done it almost immediately from pre-season and I'm not surprised because his mentality is top. I value him a lot."

Gyökeres was handed just his third start of the season in Arsenal's Champions League match against Lille on Tuesday night.

The Sweden international was withdrawn midway through the second half having made little impact on the game.

Gyökeres scored 97 times across 102 appearances for former club Sporting Lisbon, but he is yet to find the back of net in his seven games this season.

"That's a very personal question," Arteta said, when asked if Gyökeres, who struck 21 times in his debut campaign for the Gunners, is low on confidence.

"What he transmits to me is an incredible will and determination and work-rate to improve and help the team.

"That's Viktor every single day, regardless of his position, whether he scores a goal or not, and that's why he's always an option to play.

"We are trying to help him as much as possible. He has some very good moments, but it's very small margins, and scoring, or not scoring, changes the narrative."

stories.headline: 76ers, needing frontcourt help, convert 7-foot-6 Tacko Fall to two-way contract
stories.summary: The 76ers, dealing with injuries in the frontcourt, have converted center Tacko Fall to a two-way contract.
stories.body:
PHILADELPHIA -- The 76ers have converted center Tacko Fall to a two-way contract, the team announced Saturday.

Last month, the Sixers signed the 7-foot-6 center to an Exhibit 10 deal, and injuries to the frontcourt likely led to Fall getting this spot.

Ariel Hukporti, projected to be the Sixers' backup center, suffered a season-ending right Achilles tear in the preseason. Center Adem Bona, potentially the next man up, has been sidelined with a foot injury, and Dominick Barlow has battled back soreness that kept him out of the preseason.

Fall hasn't played in the NBA since the 2021-22 season, when he was with the Cleveland Cavaliers. This will be his fourth season in the NBA. He played his first two in Boston with new Sixers forward Jaylen Brown.

Fall, 30, most recently played for the Ningbo Rockets of the Chinese Basketball Association.

stories.headline: Max Verstappen clinches top-10 finish at first GT World Challenge
stories.summary: Max Verstappen fought back from 24th to ninth at the GT World Challenge after his hopes of a podium finish were derailed by a drive-through penalty.
stories.body:
Max Verstappen fought back from 24th to ninth at the GT World Challenge after his hopes of a podium finish were derailed by a drive-through penalty.

A week after claiming his second consecutive Formula One victory in as many races at the Singapore Grand Prix, the four-time world champion was back in the cockpit, this time for a three-hour endurance event in Portugal.

- 'Chucky' Verstappen is back. Luckily for Antonelli and Mercedes, it's too late

Verstappen's teammate, British driver Ben Barnicoat, delivered an encouraging opening stint to move up five places from 13th on the grid.

He handed over to compatriot Chris Lulham who progressed to sixth at the Portimao circuit in the Algarve, which will return to the F1 calendar next season.

However, Lulham was hit with a drive-through penalty when he sent Luca Stolz spinning as they duelled for fifth place.

Lulham served his sanction before Verstappen assumed driving duties, but the Dutchman's team were now out of contention and in 24th -- with only 45 minutes left.

However, Verstappen charged to 15th with a quarter of an hour remaining, and he then managed to make up another six places before the chequered flag following an impressive cameo.

Verstappen will be bidding to make it a hat-trick of F1 victories when he returns to his Red Bull at next weekend's United States Grand Prix in Austin.

stories.headline: Shakhtar's Champions League win vs. AEK was more than just a game
stories.summary: Shakhtar Donetsk haven't played at home since 2014 due to the war, and this season, their Champions League home games are at Chelsea's Stamford Bridge. Wednesday's win was a reminder of how absurd their situation is.
stories.body:
LONDON -- Take a step back and revel in the absurdity for a minute. Shakhtar Donetsk, a Ukrainian team from the Russian-speaking part of the country, are playing a Greek team, AEK Athens, in London, at Chelsea's Stamford Bridge. Technically, it's a "home game," but that concept has become rather meaningless.

Shakhtar haven't played at their home, the Donbas Arena, since May 2014, some 650 weeks ago. They turn up wherever someone will host them: Odessa, Kyiv, Kharkiv and Lviv for Ukrainian league games; Warsaw, Hamburg, Gelsenkirchen, Krakow, Ljubljana and now London for matches in European competition. Why? Because their opponents can't (or won't) travel to Ukraine, where none of the civilian airports are open, air raid sirens go off a dozen times a day, and where drones and bombs can't be trusted to distinguish between a military captain and the captain of a soccer team.

It's pretty obvious that in those circumstances, you're more than a club -- you're a symbol of defiance, an attempt to maintain some sort of normality in the face of a war that has taken more than half a million lives and displaced tens of millions more.

"We are playing for people from Ukraine all over the world," sporting director Dario Srna said. "Everywhere we've gone, they've come [to see us]. We represent Ukraine in the center of the world: we're not just playing for us. [We are] a Ukrainian team, we are not just Shakhtar."

But, of course, nothing is normal. Everything is messed up, and their mere presence in the Champions League constitutes a political dimension.

Wednesday night, Shakhtar were at Stamford Bridge, the home of Chelsea. Resourceful as ever, street vendors outside the ground hawked their off-brand scarves, except rather than "Cole Palmer," "João Pedro" and "John Terry," the names read "Pedrinho," "[Mykola] Matviyenko" and "[Valeriy] Bondar." Watching over them was a life-size cardboard cutout of Dwayne Johnson, aka The Rock, only his face was replaced by that of Ukrainian President Vladimir Zelenskyy.

Inside, visiting AEK fans -- who turned the Shed End into a two-tier wall of tifo, flags and noise -- outsing, if not outnumber, the "home" support.

Because yes, this is Shakhtar's home for the Champions League this season, a move made possible by the London club's failure to qualify for European competitions (and, probably, a need to rake in some extra rent on those empty weeknights). Ironically, Chelsea's previous owner, Roman Abramovich, was forced by the U.K. government to sell the club after the invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, because of his ties to Russian President Vladimir Putin. Abramovich holds passports from Portugal, Israel and Russia. His yachts are moored in Turkey.

Abramovich, whose mother is Ukrainian, is a complicated figure. So is Shakhtar's version of Abramovich, Rinat Akhmetov.

An ethnic Russian, but Donetsk-born and bred, Akhmetov's huge wealth from mining and energy bankrolled the club's rise to prominence prewar -- lest we forget, the likes of Willian and Fernandinho, Henrikh Mkiytaryan and Douglas Costa are all Shakhtar alums -- and keeps it alive and very much kicking today. Forbes estimates his wealth at nearly $8 billion and like most folks of that ilk, Akhmetov could easily have made different choices, decamping abroad. When the war broke out, he chose to stay, and that was not something to take for granted, given that he had previously clashed with Zelenskyy and, in the 2000s, served in parliament in the party of former pro-Russian Ukrainian President Viktor Yanukovych, whom he also backed financially.

Akhmetov broke with Yanukovych in 2014 and while his pro-Ukrainian words today are loud, his actions -- from staying in the country to tirelessly campaigning to his efforts with Shakhtar -- speak even louder.

"He can't leave Ukraine, not after seeing what he has seen," Srna says of Akhmetov. "It's impossible. He's devoted himself to this, helping the economy, helping the people. All while sleeping each night under bombs."

Many Ukrainians have no choice, which makes the actions of those who could be elsewhere all the more remarkable. It takes an unconventional type of person.

Most of Shakhtar's players are Brazilian -- lured by money, sure, but also the opportunity to showcase their talent. The coach, former Atletico Madrid and Barcelona standout Arda Turan, is Turkish. Even if you don't remember what he was like as a player, watching him prowl the technical area during the AEK game, fists clenched and eyes wild, you come to understand how this is the same guy who once got into an altercation with a pop star in an Istanbul hospital.

Srna himself is Croatian, but has been at the club -- first as a player then as sporting director -- for 23 years. He too could have left umpteen times and, in fact, he says he even turned down the chance to take over Barcelona's recruitment a decade ago.

"Ukraine and Shakhtar are in my blood," he says. "If I leave now, I couldn't live with myself."

In some ways, Srna has been here before. He was eight years old when civil war broke out in the former Yugoslavia in March 1991. The conflict that would rage for 4½ years, ripped apart communities along ethnic lines. Neighbors took up arms against neighbors. His own father woke up every day supplying baked goods for the military. If you've seen the ESPN 30 for 30 documentary "Once Brothers" about the relationship between Drazen Petrovic and Vlade Divac, well ... he lived it. Twice. Maybe that's why he soldiers on, numb to what he is experiencing.

"I have this feeling inside myself," he says. "It's a feeling I felt before [as a child experiencing war in Croatia]. But when you feel that pain and it comes back to you again, well, you're not going to have the same pain twice. I know this pain. I know this feeling ..."

Srna trails off as he searches for the right words of history -- the worst parts -- repeating itself with him in the middle of it. But then he flickers back with righteous anger.

"This is unbelievable, I can't explain it," he says. "Four-and-a-half years [this war has continued]. Bombing each other, destroying everything ... for what? For f---ing what? People die, families are destroyed, children are traumatized and grow up with psychological problems ..."

On this Wednesday night, even as Shakhtar emerge as 3-1 victors over AEK, you're reminded once again of the difficulties. The team were up at 6 a.m. on Thursday to catch a 10 o'clock flight on a plane they chartered from a budget airline taking them back to Rzeszow in Poland. They'll then board a bus back across the border into Ukraine, arriving -- best-case scenario -- at 9 p.m. local time. All this not knowing whether they'll have power and heat when they arrive, or whether they'll be making regular trips into the air raid shelter.

You want to end on a note of hope. Srna does his best to offer it, but he clearly isn't going to lie to you or to himself.

"We [Croatians] have more or less an OK relationship now with Serbia," he says. "Time [30 years have passed] is helping, generations change, it's different people. We take a step back and understand what was good, what was not good. We can't say all Serbian people are bad ... But in this moment, it's not possible to be friends with a Russian person. In time, maybe a few years, maybe many years, I don't know ... right now though, it's impossible."

Certainly more impossible than a club without a home in a country at war defying logic and competing in the Champions League against the likes of Real Madrid, who visit Stamford Bridge on Jan. 27.

One of the side effects of war is the normalization of the horrific and the absurd. Shakhtar's plight has, by necessity, normalized the absurd, in an effort to stave off the horrific.

stories.headline: AFL trade and free agency grades - Every club's report card from the 2026 transfer period
stories.summary: The 2026 AFL trade and free agency period is over. Some teams improved, some stagnated, and others, well, got worse. Here's how every team fared over the last two weeks.
stories.body:
The 2026 AFL trade and free agency period is complete. Some teams improved, some have stagnated, and others, well, seemed to have gotten worse.

READ: Every player move from the 2026 off-season

Here's how every team fared over the last two weeks:

Adelaide
Incoming: N/A

Outgoing: Jordon Butts, Luke Pedlar

2026 draft selections: 15, 32, 35, 43, 56, 92

I'm not sure what the Crows' gameplan was this trade and free agency period, but it's fair to say the club sat on its hands and did next to nothing. Losing key defender Jordon Butts to the Bulldogs obviously weakens them, while just one draft selection inside the top 30 is unlikely to provide much immediate support. Adelaide's list profile remains fine, and maybe they will surprise us all in 2027, but you just get the sense so many other clubs have passed them by over the last two weeks.

Grade: F

Brisbane
Incoming: N/A

Outgoing: Lachie Neale, Sam Marshall, Will McLachlan, Keidean Coleman

2026 draft selections: 21, 27, 28, 45, 79, 97

The Lions were the biggest winners of last year's off-season (and season!), but this year was a different story. All year it seemed a formality they would lose the services of dual Brownlow Medal winner Lachie Neale, who ultimately signed with Collingwood as a free agent. They also waved goodbye to Keidean Coleman and Sam Marshall, two players who had struggled to crack the best 23 of late. No picks inside the top 20 would be concerning for 17 other clubs, but the Lions still have so much young talent at their disposal and are primed to challenge again in 2027.

Grade: C-

Carlton
Incoming: Joel Amartey, Lachie Whitfield

Outgoing: Hudson O'Keeffe, Flynn Riley

2026 draft selections: 13, 18, 31, 50, 61, 72, 90

The Blues addressed two areas of weakness this off-season. The addition of free agent Joel Amartey provides spearhead Harry McKay with a stable forward line partner, while the Lachie Whitfield signing offers run, experience, and a kick-first option off halfback, the perfect piece to fit into Josh Fraser's system. Carlton really didn't give up much to land Whitfield, either. And barring Essendon taking a stab at talented father-son prospect Cody Walker with pick No. 1, the club has also ensured it has enough draft capital to match any bids that will come for him.

Grade: A

Collingwood
Incoming: Lachie Neale, Jesse Hogan, Flynn Riley

Outgoing: Scott Pendlebury

2026 draft selections: 11, 30, 67, 68, 70, 88

The Magpies had been crying out for a true inside midfielder, and they landed arguably the best in the competition in Lachie Neale. The two-time Brownlow Medal winner is an elite ball winner and clearance player, and should perfectly complement superstar Nick Daicos. Collingwood also signed Jesse Hogan, a man that won the Coleman Medal just two years ago, and gave up virtually nothing for him. The loss of champion Scott Pendlebury obviously stings, but you have to feel this club is in a stronger position now than it was two weeks ago.

Grade: A

Essendon
Incoming: Jack Bowes, Keidean Coleman

Outgoing: Zach Merrett, Jordan Ridley

2026 draft selections: 1, 17, 25, 80

Former skipper Zach Merrett finally got his wish of a fresh start at the Hawks, while fellow experienced player Jordan Ridley also departs the club for the Cats. The additions of Jack Bowes and Keidean Coleman are fine, but are either going to be difference makers in a side that's been languishing at the bottom of the ladder for several years? I'm not so sure. The only saving grace for the Bombers is that they hold pick No. 1. They simply have to make the most of that selection.

Grade: D

Fremantle
Incoming: Dom Bedendo

Outgoing: Nathan O'Driscoll

2026 draft selections: 19, 40, 60, 63, 78, 96

The Dockers were incredibly quiet during the trade and free agency window, but that's not exactly a bad thing. Remember, if not for Will Ashcroft and Logan Morris, Fremantle win the 2026 premiership. There was absolutely no reason for the Dockers to panic and overpay for someone after their Grand Final heartbreak, instead, this club, with its plethora of youth and talent, should feel as if it can contend for years to come. Trust the process and go again in 2027.

Grade: C

Geelong
Incoming: Toby Greene, Jordan Ridley, Rowan Marshall

Outgoing: Jack Bowes

2026 draft selections: 36, 57, 62, 75, 93

Every year the Cats just find a way to bring big names through the door, and 2026 was no exception. Rowan Marshall was tipped to join 12 months ago and finally makes the move from St Kilda to bolster the club's ruck stocks. Toby Greene adds class, experience, and unrivalled goal-kicking nous to the forward line. Jordan Ridley is a stable and still wildly underrated defensive asset. The best part? To land this trio the club only had to give up midfield depth piece Jack Bowes, and some draft capital. They won't be much of a feature at the upcoming draft, but they don't have to be. These Cats are in win-now mode.

Grade: A

Gold Coast Suns
Incoming: Scott Pendlebury, Aidan Schubert, Sam Butler

Outgoing: Ben King

2026 draft selections: 8, 85

Scott Pendlebury might be a champion of the game, but there's no denying the Suns just got worse. The addition of 38-year-old Pendlebury doesn't outweigh the seismic loss of spearhead Ben King, a man who has booted 230 goals over the last four seasons. How do they replace him? Perhaps it's the incoming Aidan Schubert, but he's years away from having a real impact. Making matters worse, it seems Brownlow medallist Matt Rowell is likely to request a trade back to Victoria at the end of next season. This club is in a real precarious spot right now. A penny for Christian Petracca's thoughts...

Grade: C-

GWS Giants
Incoming: N/A

Outgoing: Toby Greene, Kieren Briggs, Jesse Hogan, Lachie Whitfield

2026 draft selections: 9, 20, 26, 59, 77, 86

Just two years ago Toby Greene, Kieren Briggs, Jesse Hogan, and Lachie Whitfield were probably four of the Giants' most important players. None of them remain at the club after an action-packed trade and free agency window, with GWS instead opting to clear out and trust the youth underneath. It's a move that will either make the Giants look like geniuses or total fools, but even those who are incredibly bullish about the approach would concede there is likely to be some pain on the immediate horizon.

Grade: D

Hawthorn
Incoming: Zach Merrett, Ben King, Josh Goater

Outgoing: Finn Maginness, Aidan Schubert, Sam Butler, Bodie Ryan

2026 draft selections: 29, 37, 71, 94

The Hawks should probably be the 2027 flag favourites after a whirlwind two weeks that's seen them finally land former Essendon skipper Zach Merrett, as well as Ben King. Merrett adds depth, experience, and A-grade ball use to Hawthorn's midfield group, while King provides a focal point in attack, taking the burden off the ageing Jack Gunston. Sure, Hawthorn gave up some depth, but their best 23 has improved out of sight and they still have draft collateral over the next few years to ensure talent keeps coming through the door.

Grade: A+

Melbourne
Incoming: Zane Duursma, Will McLachlan, Bodie Ryan

Outgoing: Jack Viney, Trent Rivers

2026 draft selections: 4, 14, 48, 52

Just about everyone panicked when the Demons farewelled premiership heroes Christian Petracca and Clayton Oliver last year, and look how that turned out. This club seems to have a plan for the future and it isn't prepared to compromise on what it wants. Melbourne has nailed its draft picks in recent times and with selections four and 14 this year, you'd expect two more highly talented prospects to join the ranks. Who knows if Zane Duursma will work out, but they've landed him for a fraction of what the Kangaroos gave up at the draft three years ago. It's a low risk punt worth taking.

Grade: C

North Melbourne
Incoming: Nick Blakey

Outgoing: Zane Duursma, Josh Goater

2026 draft selections: 33, 49, 66, 74, 84

Credit to the Kangaroos, they finally landed a big name. The only problem is I'm not sure Nick Blakey is the superstar many are claiming. There's no doubt Blakey will add drive and dash off halfback, but is he the player you look to in the closing stages of a tight game? North also gave up a truckload of future draft capital to get him through the door which will hurt them in the coming years. And then there's the Zane Duursma fiasco. Losing a player the club invested pick No. 4 in just three years ago is an unmitigated disaster. With no selections inside the top 30 this year, it will be a rare draft without the Roos being a major player.

Grade: C+

Port Adelaide
Incoming: Luke Pedlar

Outgoing: Zak Butters

2026 draft selections: 7, 12, 22, 24, 34, 46, 65

You're never going to feel great when a player of Zak Butters' class and calibre walks out the door, but the silver lining for Port Adelaide is that Dougie Cochrane should be set to walk back in. The academy talent is the consensus best player in the upcoming draft and the Power are in a position to match any bids on their man. Expect Port to be heavily involved in the draft over the next couple of years as they look to rebuild around the likes of Cochrane, Connor Rozee, and Jason Horne-Francis.

Grade: B

Richmond
Incoming: Kieren Briggs, Nathan O'Driscoll

Outgoing: N/A

2026 draft selections: 2, 5, 44, 81

The Tigers found Toby Nankervis' successor in Kieren Briggs, who crosses from the Giants as a free agent. That's a nice win. Nathan O'Driscoll was unable to find a place in Fremantle's best team of late but should receive far more opportunity in the black and yellow jumper in 2027. Richmond has two more picks inside the top five, though they are likely to be shuffled down a few spots with bid matching on Dougie Cochrane and Cody Walker, and they simply must nail them. Even still, this side will remain incredibly young in 2027.

Grade: C

St Kilda
Incoming: Sam Marshall

Outgoing: Rowan Marshall

2026 draft selections: 10, 16, 41, 51, 69, 87

The Saints went all-in last year, signing Tom De Koning, Jack Silvagni, Liam Ryan, and Sam Flanders. They weren't nearly as busy this off-season, and few expected them to be. Long-time ruck Rowan Marshall departs the club for the Cats, while Sam Marshall joins and should bolster their midfield stocks. Outside of that, St Kilda will be hoping to cash in with their two first round draft selections. If not, it could spell the end of Nasiah Wanganeen-Milera's tenure. This team wouldn't want to be starting 2027 slowly...

Grade: C

Sydney Swans
Incoming: N/A

Outgoing: Joel Amartey, Nick Blakey

2026 draft selections: 6, 38, 39, 47, 54, 76, 95

Two best 23 players departed the Swans this past fortnight with halfback Nick Blakey being traded to the Kangaroos and key forward Joel Amartey signing with the Blues as a free agent. Don't forget, Callum Mills is unlikely to suit up for the entire year after suffering an ACL injury during this year's finals campaign. That's three best 23 players to replace! Who knows what's happening with Isaac Heeney and Chad Warner? Swans fans will be praying for a hit with pick No. 6 at the upcoming draft to soften the blow.

Grade: C-

West Coast Eagles
Incoming: Jack Viney, Trent Rivers

Outgoing: N/A

2026 draft selections: 3, 23, 58, 64, 73, 82

It's clear the Eagles don't want to take the same approach as the Tigers and rely solely on the kids. Instead, they're continuing to add experienced pieces around their young talent in an effort to ease the rebuild and avoid a nosedive in morale. Jack Viney and Trent Rivers add premiership experience to the club and they haven't had to give up too much to get them. West Coast will feature prominently at November's draft with pick No. 3, 23, as well as a compensation pick in the likely scenario that the club's first selection is pushed back by a bid.

Grade: C+

Western Bulldogs
Incoming: Jordon Butts, Finn Maginness, Hudson O'Keeffe, Zak Butters

Outgoing: N/A

2026 draft selections: 42, 53, 55, 83, 89, 91

The Bulldogs now possess the most dynamic midfield trio in the game with Zak Butters joining skipper Marcus Bontempelli and Ed Richards in the red, white, and blue. It's a marquee signing for Luke Beveridge's team that simply has to put them into premiership contention. Jordon Butts also joins the club and will bolster what's traditionally been a weaker defensive unit. Don't forget about key forward star Sam Darcy, who will return from a season-ending ACL injury.

Grade: A+
